Agents & data evaluation

AgentFAIR

A multi-agent workflow for evaluating the findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reusability of geospatial datasets.

Preprint · 2026·Preprint
Read preprintExplore code
On this pageThe problemMy contributionDesign decisionsEvaluationLimitationsPaper & resources

The problem

FAIRness assessment involves interpreting metadata, checking evidence, and applying criteria consistently across heterogeneous geospatial datasets. Repeating that work manually is time-consuming.

My contribution

As co-first and corresponding author, I worked with a supervised student on a multi-agent approach to structured FAIRness evaluation. The implementation connects metadata extraction, 13 FAIR sub-principle evaluators, and critic feedback loops through a LangGraph workflow, with a FastAPI service and a React dashboard.

Design decisions

Organize around explicit criteria

Separate the dimensions of findability, accessibility, interoperability, and reusability so that an assessment can be understood criterion by criterion.

Keep the evidence visible

Treat an assessment as a structured evaluation with supporting observations, rather than only a fluent explanation.

Make evaluation part of the workflow

Examine the behavior of the assessment process itself, including consistency and the interpretation of dataset metadata.

Evaluation & outcomes

The public research implementation includes a multi-agent workflow and an interactive evaluation dashboard. The linked preprint presents the methodology and evaluation; the archived software record provides an additional release reference.

FAIRfindable · accessible · interoperable · reusable

What the results depend on

An agent-generated assessment depends on available metadata, access to evidence, the chosen criteria, and model behavior. The public repository does not include every benchmark artifact needed to reproduce all manuscript results.
